title: Cables, colour, lace and short rows: four skills that sell

say: Cables, colour, lace and short rows: four skills that sell.
This is the video for module two of Advanced Knitting and Crochet.
This module adds four knitting techniques that turn plain fabric into products people notice. Cables give texture. Colourwork gives pattern.

panel.heading: Plain fabric into products people notice
items: Cables for texture
Colourwork for pattern
Lace for light summer pieces
Short rows for shaping real bodies

say: Lace makes light pieces for warm weather. And short rows shape a top to fit a real body.

say: A cable is a few stitches knitted out of order. Slip the stated stitches purlwise onto a short cable needle, and hold it in front or at the back, as the abbreviation says.

panel.heading: Each crossing is four small moves
items: Slip stitches purlwise to cable needle
Hold it in front or at the back
Knit the next stitches firmly
Knit the stitches from the cable needle
Hang a marker on the crossing row

say: Knit the next stitches firmly from the left needle, then knit the ones from the cable needle, pulling the yarn snug.

panel.heading: Each crossing is four small moves
items: Slip stitches purlwise to cable needle
Hold it in front or at the back
Knit the next stitches firmly
Knit the stitches from the cable needle
Hang a marker on the crossing row

say: Hang a marker on the crossing row, so you can count rows to the next crossing.
Remember: a front cross leans left, a back cross leans right. Put C6B on the left rope and C6F on the right, and they mirror.
Cables pull fabric in, so always swatch the cable pattern itself.

panel.heading: Each crossing is four small moves
items: Slip stitches purlwise to cable needle

Knit the stitches from the cable needle
Hang a marker on the crossing row
panel.rule: Front goes left, back goes right.

say: There are three colourwork methods. Stripes change colour at the start of a row. Carry the yarn up the side for narrow stripes, and cut it for wide ones.

cards.d: Change colour at the start of a row. Carry yarn up the side for narrow stripes, cut it for wide ones.
One bobbin for each block of colour. Twist the old and new yarn at every change.
Two colours in a row. Keep floats loose, and catch any float longer than about 5 stitches.

say: Intarsia is for large blocks and letters. Each area of colour has its own bobbin. At every change, pick up the new colour from under the old one, so they twist and no hole forms.

cards.d: Change colour at the start of a row. Carry yarn up the side for narrow stripes, cut it for wide ones.
One bobbin for each block of colour. Twist the old and new yarn at every change.
Two colours in a row. Keep floats loose, and catch any float longer than about 5 stitches.

say: Stranded knitting uses two colours in a row, and the unused one floats behind. Tight floats pucker the fabric. Catch any float longer than about 5 stitches. Stranded fabric is double thickness, so in hot weather use it for bags and accessories.

cards.d: Change colour at the start of a row. Carry yarn up the side for narrow stripes, cut it for wide ones.
One bobbin for each block of colour. Twist the old and new yarn at every change.

say: For example, Kemi in Lagos wants a striped scarf about 160 cm long. Her row gauge is 30 rows per 10 cm, so she needs 480 rows.

panel.heading: Kemi plans a striped scarf
items: 160 cm x 3 rows per cm = 480 rows
6 rows each of A, B, C = 18 per repeat
Each colour about 300 g / 3 = 100 g
Buy 2 balls of each, plus 1 extra

say: Her sequence is 6 rows each of three colours, 18 rows per repeat. 480 divided by 18 is 26.7, so she rounds up to 27 repeats and ends on a full stripe.

say: A plain scarf uses about 300 g, so each colour needs about 100 g. Yarn comes in 50 g balls, so she buys 2 of each, plus 1 extra. She buys 7 balls instead of guessing.

say: Lace is fabric with holes placed on purpose. A yarn over adds a stitch and makes a hole. k2tog removes one and leans right. ssk removes one and leans left.

panel.heading: Check that every repeat balances
items: yo adds 1 stitch and makes a hole
k2tog removes 1, leans right
ssk removes 1, leans left
Net change 0: the scarf stays 47 wide

say: For example, Ruth in Abuja counts one repeat of her scarf: yarn over, ssk, knit, k2tog, yarn over, knit. The net change is zero, so her 47 stitches stay 47 all the way up.
Each yarn over adds a stitch, so pair it with a decrease.

panel.heading: Check that every repeat balances
items: yo adds 1 stitch and makes a hole
k2tog removes 1, leans right
ssk removes 1, leans left
Net change 0: the scarf stays 47 wide
panel.rule: Each yarn over adds a stitch. Pair it with a decrease.

say: Keep these habits. Count stitches on every right-side row. Thread a lifeline every 10 to 20 rows, so a mistake costs minutes, not days. When Ruth dropped a yarn over on row 53, she pulled back only to her lifeline at row 40.
Put a marker between repeats, read the chart with a ruler, and always block lace before you judge it. Unblocked lace looks crumpled.

panel.heading: Habits that prevent tears
items: Count stitches every right-side row
Lifeline every 10 to 20 rows
Marker between each repeat
Read the chart with a ruler
Block before judging

say: A short row is a row you do not finish. You turn early and go back, so one area gains length. For example, Ifeoma in Enugu needs about 5 cm more length over the bust.

panel.heading: Ifeoma's bust dart
items: Needs 5 cm more length at the front
5 cm x 2.8 rows per cm = 14 rows
14 rows = 7 pairs of short rows
Turns about 4 stitches apart
One full row each way hides the turns

say: Her gauge is 28 rows per 10 cm. 5 times 2.8 is 14 rows. Each pair of short rows adds 2 rows, so she needs 7 pairs.

panel.heading: Ifeoma's bust dart
items: Needs 5 cm more length at the front
5 cm x 2.8 rows per cm = 14 rows
14 rows = 7 pairs of short rows
Turns about 4 stitches apart
One full row each way hides the turns

say: She spaces the turns about 4 stitches apart, from each side edge, then works one full row each way to hide them. Now her hem hangs level.
Stop the turns a little before the bust point, or the dart can form a pointed bump.

panel.heading: Ifeoma's bust dart
items: Needs 5 cm more length at the front
5 cm x 2.8 rows per cm = 14 rows
14 rows = 7 pairs of short rows
Turns about 4 stitches apart
One full row each way hides the turns
panel.rule: Each pair of short rows adds 2 rows. Stop before the bust point.

say: To remember. Front cross leans left, back cross leans right. Twist your yarns at every intarsia change. Catch long floats. Pair every yarn over with a decrease. And divide the extra rows by 2 to get your pairs of short rows.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Front cross leans left, back leans right
Intarsia: twist yarns at every change
Catch floats longer than about 5 stitches
Pair every yarn over with a decrease
Extra rows / 2 = pairs of short rows
